title: מַסֶּכֶת אָבוֹת — פֶּרֶק חֲמִישִׁי
part: Chapter 5 · The numbered sayings, Ben Bag Bag and Ben He He
draftNote: The text follows the Wikisource transcription of the Kaufmann manuscript, apart from the editorial steps named in the source note; the prepared audio is being built; a check against the manuscript photographs is still to come. Use ⚑ correction on any mishnah to report a problem.
source: Text: the Kaufmann manuscript of the Mishnah (Budapest, Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, Kaufmann A 50), fols. 169r–173v, from the diplomatic transcription on Hebrew Wikisource (כתב יד קאופמן למשנה/מסכת אבות, CC BY-SA 4.0), which records the work of the later hands. The vowel points are the manuscript's own. Where it leaves a letter of a pointed word bare, the editor has supplied the point, and the mishnah's note lists every such word; words the manuscript leaves wholly unpointed stay unpointed. Reading text: the manuscript as corrected. Letters the manuscript erases are omitted; corrections and additions by later hands, including marginal ones, are printed; marginal variant readings (נ״א) are left out. Words the scribe broke across a line end are rejoined. The scribe's abbreviations are kept, marked with a geresh (׳), and expanded in the glossary. The transcription writes Kaufmann's ḥolam, which sits over the preceding letter, as a dot on that letter; it is given here as an ordinary ḥolam. Mishnayot are numbered as in the standard printed editions; where Kaufmann divides differently, or lacks a mishnah, the note says so. Romanization: simplified, following Modern Israeli pronunciation. Pronunciation convention: Modern Israeli Hebrew applied to Kaufmann's vowels — an admitted choice, since the manuscript's pointing reflects an older Palestinian tradition. Translations made fresh from the Hebrew and Aramaic; no modern translation consulted. Audio: Google Cloud TTS, Modern Israeli Hebrew voice, reading the pointed text; abbreviations are read in full (או׳ as אוֹמֵר, שנ׳ as שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר, the divine name as Adonay).
about: Avot, "Fathers", is the tractate of the Mishnah made up of maxims; the rest of the Mishnah is law. It opens with the chain of tradition from Moses at Sinai to the Men of the Great Assembly, then gives the sayings of the sages from the early pairs down to the generation of the Mishnah's editor, Rabbi Judah the Prince. The Mishnah was compiled around 200 CE. Many communities read Avot a chapter at a time on Sabbath afternoons between Passover and Shavuot, and often through the summer, adding a sixth chapter, Kinyan Torah, to make six weeks. Chapters 1–5 here follow a single manuscript, the Kaufmann codex, probably copied in Italy in the eleventh or twelfth century and the best witness to the Mishnah's own Hebrew. It reads differently from the familiar printed text in many small places, and the notes point them out.

sentences.t: בַּעֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם וּמַה תַּלְמוּד וַהֲלֹא מַאֲמָר אֶחָד הָיָה יָכוֹל לְהִיבָּרוֹת אֶלָּא לְהִיפָּרַע מִן הָרְשָׁעִים שֶׁהֶן מְאַבְּדִין אֶת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁנִּבְרָא בַעֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת וְלִיתֵּן שָׂכָר טוֹב לַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁהֶן מְקַיְּימִים אֶת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁנִבְרָא בַעֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת
sentences.tr: Ba-asara ma'amarot nivra ha-olam. U-ma talmud? Va-halo ma'amar eḥad haya yakhol lehibarot! Ela lehipara min ha-resha'im she-hen me'abdin et ha-olam she-nivra va-asara ma'amarot, ve-liten sakhar tov la-tsadikim she-hen mekaymim et ha-olam she-nivra va-asara ma'amarot.
sentences.l: By ten sayings the world was created. And what does-it-teach? And was not one saying able (for it) to be-created? But (it was) to exact-payment from the wicked, who destroy the world that was created by ten sayings, and to give good reward to the righteous, who sustain the world that was created by ten sayings.
sentences.i: The world was created through ten utterances. What does this teach? Could it not have been created with a single utterance? It was done this way to exact payment from the wicked, who destroy a world created through ten utterances, and to give a good reward to the righteous, who sustain a world created through ten utterances.
sentences.n: The ten utterances are God's commands in the creation story of Genesis 1, where 'And God said' recurs. The chapter is built from such numbered lists: ten, then seven, then four. לְהִיפָּרַע מִן is a creditor's word, 'to collect payment from'. מְאַבְּדִין and שֶׁהֶן show two Mishnaic habits you met in chapter 1: plural -in, and -hen for -hem. The printed editions read וּמַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר, 'and what does it come to teach', and בְּמַאֲמָר אֶחָד, 'with one utterance'; Kaufmann has the shorter מַה תַּלְמוּד and no bet. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: אֶחָד, שֶׁנִּבְרָא.

sentences.t: עֲשָׂרָה דוֹרוֹת מֵאָדָם וְעַד נֹוַח לְהוֹדִיַע כַּמָּה אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם לְפָנָיו שֶׁכָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת הָיוּ מַכְעִיסִים לְפָנָיו עַד שֶׁהֵבִיא עֲלֵיהֶם אֶת הַמַּבּוּל עֲשָׁרָה דוֹרוֹת מִנֹּוַח וְעַד אַבְרָהָם אֲבִינוּ לְהוֹדִיַע כַּמָּה אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם לְפָנָיו שֶׁכָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת הָיוּ מַכְעִיסִים לְפָנָיו עַד שֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וְקִיבֵּל שְׂכַר כּוּלָם
sentences.tr: Asara dorot me-Adam ve-ad Noaḥ, lehodia kama erekh apayim lefanav, she-kol ha-dorot hayu makh'isim lefanav, ad she-hevi aleihem et ha-mabul. Asara dorot mi-Noaḥ ve-ad Avraham avinu, lehodia kama erekh apayim lefanav, she-kol ha-dorot hayu makh'isim lefanav, ad she-ba Avraham avinu ve-kibel skhar kulam.
sentences.l: Ten generations from Adam and until Noah — to make known how-great is the length of anger before Him, for all the generations were provoking before Him, until He brought upon them the Flood. Ten generations from Noah and until Abraham our father — to make known how-great is the length of anger before Him, for all the generations were provoking before Him, until Abraham our father came and received the reward of them all.
sentences.i: There were ten generations from Adam to Noah, to show how patient He is: every one of those generations provoked Him, until He brought the Flood upon them. There were ten generations from Noah to Abraham our father, to show how patient He is: every one of those generations provoked Him, until Abraham our father came and received the reward that all of them had lost.
sentences.n: אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם, literally 'length of nostrils', is the biblical idiom for patience: anger was pictured as heat in the nose, and a long nose takes long to heat. The two genealogies are Genesis 5 and 11. 'Received the reward of them all': the merit the earlier generations forfeited passed to Abraham. לְפָנָיו, 'before Him', lets the Mishnah speak of God without naming Him. Kaufmann writes Noah's name נֹוַח, with a vav after the ḥolam, and puts the furtive pataḥ of לְהוֹדִיַע under the yod. In Kaufmann this mishnah and the next form a single section.

sentences.t: עֲשָׂרָה נִיסְיוֹנוֹת מִתְנַסָּה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וְעָמַד בְּכוּלָּם לְהוֹדִיַע כַּמָּה הִיא חִיבָּתוֹ שֶׁלְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ:
sentences.tr: Asara nisyonot mitnase Avraham avinu ve-amad be-khulam, lehodia kama hi ḥibato shel Avraham avinu.
sentences.l: Ten trials Abraham our father is-tested, and he stood in all of them — to make known how-great is the love of Abraham our father.
sentences.i: Abraham our father was tested with ten trials and withstood them all, to show how great was the love for Abraham our father.
sentences.n: חִיבָּתוֹ is 'the love of him': God's love for Abraham, or Abraham's for God — the phrase allows both. The rabbis listed the ten trials differently; every list ends with the binding of Isaac (Genesis 22). עָמַד בְּ, 'stood in', means withstood. Kaufmann has the participle מִתְנַסָּה, 'is tested', where the printed editions have the perfect נִתְנַסָּה, 'was tested'.

sentences.t: עֲשָׂרָה נִיסִּים נֶעֱשׂוּ לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְמִצְרַיִם וַעֲשָׁרָה עַל הַיָּם עֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת הֵבִיא הַקָּבָּ״הֻ עַל הַמִּצְרִיִּים בְּמִצְרַיִם וְעֶשֶׂר עַל הַיָּם עֲשָׂרָה נִיסְיוֹנוֹת נִיסּוּ אֲבוֹתֵ׳ אֶת הַמָּקוֹם בַּמִּדְבָּר שנ׳ וַיְנַסּוּ אֹתִי זֶה עֶשֶׂר פְּעָמִים וְלֹא שָׁמְעוּ בְּקוֹלִי:
sentences.tr: Asara nisim na'asu la-avoteinu be-Mitsrayim va-asara al ha-yam. Eser makot hevi ha-Kadosh barukh hu al ha-Mitsriyim be-Mitsrayim ve-eser al ha-yam. Asara nisyonot nisu avoteinu et ha-Makom ba-midbar, she-ne'emar: va-yenasu oti ze eser pe'amim ve-lo shamu be-koli.
sentences.l: Ten miracles were done for our fathers in Egypt, and ten at the Sea. Ten plagues the Holy One, blessed be He, brought on the Egyptians in Egypt, and ten at the Sea. Ten trials our fathers tried the Omnipresent in the wilderness, as it is said: and they have tried Me these ten times and have not listened to My voice.
sentences.i: Ten miracles were performed for our ancestors in Egypt, and ten at the Sea. Ten plagues the Holy One, blessed be He, brought upon the Egyptians in Egypt, and ten at the Sea. With ten trials our ancestors tried the Omnipresent in the wilderness, as it is said: 'They have tried Me these ten times and have not obeyed My voice' (Numbers 14:22).
sentences.n: הַמָּקוֹם, literally 'the Place', is a rabbinic name for God: 'the Omnipresent'. The verse is Numbers 14:22, God's words after the spies' report; זֶה עֶשֶׂר פְּעָמִים there means 'ten times now', and the Mishnah takes the number at its word and finds ten episodes in the wilderness stories. The ten plagues 'at the Sea' carry the count of blows against Egypt on to the drowning at the Sea of Reeds. Two abbreviations: אֲבוֹתֵ׳ for אֲבוֹתֵינוּ, 'our fathers', and שנ׳ for שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר. In Kaufmann a he after וְעֶשֶׂר was erased. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: נִיסּוּ.
sentences.say: עֲשָׂרָה נִיסִּים נֶעֱשׂוּ לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְמִצְרַיִם וַעֲשָׁרָה עַל הַיָּם עֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת הֵבִיא הַקָּדוֹשׁ-בָּרוּךְ-הוּא עַל הַמִּצְרִיִּים בְּמִצְרַיִם וְעֶשֶׂר עַל הַיָּם עֲשָׂרָה נִיסְיוֹנוֹת נִיסּוּ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ אֶת הַמָּקוֹם בַּמִּדְבָּר שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיְנַסּוּ אֹתִי זֶה עֶשֶׂר פְּעָמִים וְלֹא שָׁמְעוּ בְּקוֹלִי:

sentences.t: עֲשָׂרָה נִיסִּים נֶעֱשׂוּ בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּש לֹא הִפִּילָה אִשָּׁה מֵרֵיַח בְּשַׂר קוֹדֶש מֵעוֹלָם לֹא הִיסְרִיַח בְּשַׂר קוֹדֶשׁ מֵעוֹלָם לֹא אֵירַע קֶרִי לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל בְיוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים לֹא נִרְאָה זְבוּב בְּבֵית המטבחים לֹא נִימְצָא פְסוּל בַּעוֹמֶר וּבִשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם וּבְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים לֹא כִיבּוּ גְשָׁמִים אֶת הַמַּעֲרָכָה לֹא נָצְחָה הָרוּחַ אֶת עַמּוּד עשָׁן עוֹמְדִים צְפוּפִין וּמִשְׁתַּחֲוִים רִווּחִים לֹא הִיזִּיק נָחָשׁ וְעַקְרָב בִּירוּשָׁלִַם לֹא אָמַ׳ אָדָם לַחֲבֵירוֹ צַר לִי הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁאָלִין בִּירוּשָׁלִַם:
sentences.tr: Asara nisim na'asu be-veit ha-mikdash: lo hipila isha me-reiaḥ besar kodesh me-olam; lo hisriaḥ besar kodesh me-olam; lo eira keri le-khohen gadol be-yom ha-kipurim; lo nir'a zvuv be-veit ha-mitbaḥayim; lo nimtsa psul ba-omer u-vi-shtei ha-leḥem u-ve-leḥem ha-panim; lo kibu gshamim et ha-ma'arakha; lo natsḥa ha-ruaḥ et amud ashan; omdim tsfufin u-mishtaḥavim rivuḥim; lo hizik naḥash ve-akrav bi-Yrushalayim; lo amar adam la-ḥavero: tsar li ha-makom she-alin bi-Yrushalayim.
sentences.l: Ten miracles were done in the House of the Sanctuary: a woman did not miscarry from the smell of holy meat, ever; holy meat did not go-putrid, ever; an emission did not befall the high priest on the Day of Atonement; a fly was not seen in the house of slaughtering; a defect was not found in the Omer and in the two loaves and in the bread of the Presence; rains did not put-out the altar-pile; the wind did not overcome the pillar of smoke; (they were) standing crowded and bowing-down (with) spaces; snake and scorpion did not harm in Jerusalem; a man did not say to his fellow: the place is tight for me that I should lodge in Jerusalem.
sentences.i: Ten miracles were performed in the Temple. No woman ever miscarried from the smell of the sacrificial meat. The sacrificial meat never went bad. The high priest never had a seminal emission on the Day of Atonement. No fly was seen in the slaughtering area. No defect was found in the Omer, in the two loaves, or in the showbread. The rains never put out the altar fire. The wind never overcame the column of smoke. The people stood pressed together, yet when they bowed down there was room to spare. Snake and scorpion never did harm in Jerusalem. And no one ever said to his fellow, 'It is too crowded for me to lodge in Jerusalem.'
sentences.n: Each miracle answers a real hazard of a busy sanctuary: the smell of roasting meat, which a pregnant woman might crave and be unable to eat; flies around the slaughter; a high priest made impure by a nocturnal emission on the one day only he could serve; rain on an open-air altar. The Omer is the barley offering brought at Passover (Leviticus 23:10), the two loaves the wheat offering of Shavuot (Leviticus 23:17), the bread of the Presence the loaves set out each Sabbath (Leviticus 24:5–9). On the pilgrim festivals the Temple court was packed, yet everyone found room to prostrate. Kaufmann lists the miracles in a different order from the printed editions, and has 'did not put out the altar-pile' where the printed text has 'the fire of the wood of the altar-pile'. The manuscript was worked over here: הִסְרִיַח is written over an erasure; הַמִּטְבָּחַיִם was added in the margin by a second hand, unvocalized; a he added before עָשָׁן, making it 'the smoke', was later erased; and רִווּחִים was rewritten by a second hand over an erasure. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: הַמִּקְדָּש, לְכֹהֵן, בְיוֹם, כִיבּוּ, בִּירוּשָׁלִַם.
sentences.say: עֲשָׂרָה נִיסִּים נֶעֱשׂוּ בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּש לֹא הִפִּילָה אִשָּׁה מֵרֵיַח בְּשַׂר קוֹדֶש מֵעוֹלָם לֹא הִיסְרִיַח בְּשַׂר קוֹדֶשׁ מֵעוֹלָם לֹא אֵירַע קֶרִי לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל בְיוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים לֹא נִרְאָה זְבוּב בְּבֵית המטבחים לֹא נִימְצָא פְסוּל בַּעוֹמֶר וּבִשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם וּבְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים לֹא כִיבּוּ גְשָׁמִים אֶת הַמַּעֲרָכָה לֹא נָצְחָה הָרוּחַ אֶת עַמּוּד עשָׁן עוֹמְדִים צְפוּפִין וּמִשְׁתַּחֲוִים רִווּחִים לֹא הִיזִּיק נָחָשׁ וְעַקְרָב בִּירוּשָׁלִַם לֹא אָמַר אָדָם לַחֲבֵירוֹ צַר לִי הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁאָלִין בִּירוּשָׁלִַם:

sentences.t: עֲשָׂרָה דְבָרִים נִבְרְאוּ בֵין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת פִּי הָאָרֶץ וּפִי הַבְּאֵר וּפִי הָאָתוֹן וְהַקֶּשֶׁת וְהַמָּן וְהַמַּטֶּה וְהַשָּׁמִיר וְהַכְּתָב וְהַמִּכְתָּב וְהַלֻּחוֹת וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְ׳ אַף הַמַּזִּיקִין וּקְבוּרָתוֹ שֶׁלְמֹשֶׁה וְאֵילֹו שֶׁלְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְ׳ אַף צָבָת בִצְבַת הָעֲשׂוּיָה:
sentences.tr: Asara dvarim nivre'u bein ha-shmashot: pi ha-arets, u-fi ha-be'er, u-fi ha-aton, ve-ha-keshet, ve-ha-man, ve-ha-mate, ve-ha-shamir, ve-ha-ktav, ve-ha-mikhtav, ve-ha-luḥot. Ve-yesh omrim: af ha-mazikin, u-kvurato shel Moshe, ve-eilo shel Avraham avinu. Ve-yesh omrim: af tsavat bi-tsvat ha-asuya.
sentences.l: Ten things were created between the suns: the mouth of the earth, and the mouth of the well, and the mouth of the she-ass, and the bow, and the manna, and the staff, and the shamir, and the writing, and the inscription, and the tablets. And some say: also the harmful-ones, and the grave of Moses, and the ram of Abraham our father. And some say: also tongs, with tongs (that are) made.
sentences.i: Ten things were created at twilight on the eve of the first Sabbath: the mouth of the earth, the mouth of the well, the mouth of the donkey, the rainbow, the manna, the staff, the shamir, the script, the writing, and the tablets. Some say: also the demons, the grave of Moses, and the ram of Abraham our father. And some say: also tongs, which are made with tongs.
sentences.n: 'Between the suns' is twilight — here the twilight that closed the sixth day of creation, just before the first Sabbath. The things that later break the order of nature were made then, as part of creation. The mouth of the earth swallowed Korah (Numbers 16:32); the well followed Israel in the wilderness (Numbers 21:16–18); the donkey's mouth spoke to Balaam (Numbers 22:28); the bow is the rainbow after the Flood (Genesis 9:13). The shamir, in rabbinic legend, is a creature that cut the Temple's stones, since no iron tool could touch them. The writing and the inscription are the letters on the Tablets and their engraving (Exodus 32:16). Moses' grave is the one 'no man knows' (Deuteronomy 34:6); the ram is the one Abraham offered in Isaac's place (Genesis 22:13). Tongs are forged with tongs, so the first pair had to come from God. Additions in Kaufmann: דְבָרִים and אָבִינוּ in the margin, and as raised letters the he of הַמַּזִּיקִין, the vav of וְאֵילוֹ and the he of הָעֲשׂוּיָה. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: וְאֵילֹו.
sentences.say: עֲשָׂרָה דְבָרִים נִבְרְאוּ בֵין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת פִּי הָאָרֶץ וּפִי הַבְּאֵר וּפִי הָאָתוֹן וְהַקֶּשֶׁת וְהַמָּן וְהַמַּטֶּה וְהַשָּׁמִיר וְהַכְּתָב וְהַמִּכְתָּב וְהַלֻּחוֹת וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים אַף הַמַּזִּיקִין וּקְבוּרָתוֹ שֶׁלְמֹשֶׁה וְאֵילֹו שֶׁלְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים אַף צָבָת בִצְבַת הָעֲשׂוּיָה:

sentences.t: שִׁבְעָה דְבָרִים בַּגּוֹלֶם וְשִׁבְעָה בֶחָכָם הֶחָכָם אֵינוּ מְדַבֵּר לִפְנֵי מִי שֶׁהוּא גָדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ וְאֵינוּ נִכְנַס לְתוֹךְ דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוֹ וְאֵינוּ נִבְהַל לְהָשִׁיב שֹׁאֵל כַּהֲלָכָה וּמֵשִׁיב כָּעִינְיָן וְאוֹמֵ׳ עַל רִאשׁוֹן רִאשׁוֹן וְעַל אַחֲרוֹן אַחֲרוֹן וְעַל מָה שֶּׁלֹּא שָׁמַע אוֹמֵ׳ לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי וּמוֹדֶה עַל הָאֶמֶת וְחִילּוּפֵיהֶן בַּגּוֹלֶם:
sentences.tr: Shiv'a dvarim ba-golem ve-shiv'a ve-ḥakham. Ha-ḥakham einu medaber lifnei mi she-hu gadol mimenu, ve-einu nikhnas le-tokh divrei ḥavero, ve-einu nivhal lehashiv; sho'el ka-halakha u-meshiv ka-inyan, ve-omer al rishon rishon ve-al aḥaron aḥaron, ve-al ma she-lo shama omer: lo shamati, u-mode al ha-emet. Ve-ḥilufeihen ba-golem.
sentences.l: Seven things (are) in the clod and seven in the wise-man. The wise-man does not speak before one who is greater than he, and does not enter into the midst of his fellow's words, and is not hasty to answer; he asks according to the law and answers according to the subject; and he says about first, first, and about last, last; and about what he did not hear he says: I did not hear; and he admits to the truth. And their opposites (are) in the clod.
sentences.i: There are seven marks of the uncultivated man and seven of the wise man. The wise man does not speak before someone greater than he is; he does not break in while his fellow is speaking; he is not hasty to answer; he asks to the point of the law and answers to the point of the question; he deals with first things first and last things last; about what he has not heard he says, 'I have not heard'; and he concedes the truth. In the uncultivated man you find the opposite of each.
sentences.n: גּוֹלֶם is a shapeless lump, raw material a craftsman has not yet worked — here a person whose mind learning has not shaped. מוֹדֶה עַל הָאֶמֶת: he concedes when the other side is right. אֵינוּ is Kaufmann's regular spelling of אֵינוֹ, 'he is not'. The printed editions have the two clauses the other way round — 'asks to the point and answers according to the law' — and say the greater person is greater 'in wisdom and in years'.
sentences.say: שִׁבְעָה דְבָרִים בַּגּוֹלֶם וְשִׁבְעָה בֶחָכָם הֶחָכָם אֵינוּ מְדַבֵּר לִפְנֵי מִי שֶׁהוּא גָדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ וְאֵינוּ נִכְנַס לְתוֹךְ דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוֹ וְאֵינוּ נִבְהַל לְהָשִׁיב שֹׁאֵל כַּהֲלָכָה וּמֵשִׁיב כָּעִינְיָן וְאוֹמֵר עַל רִאשׁוֹן רִאשׁוֹן וְעַל אַחֲרוֹן אַחֲרוֹן וְעַל מָה שֶּׁלֹּא שָׁמַע אוֹמֵר לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי וּמוֹדֶה עַל הָאֶמֶת וְחִילּוּפֵיהֶן בַּגּוֹלֶם:

sentences.t: שִׁבְעָה מִינֵי פוּרְעָנִיּוֹת בָּאִים עַל שִׁבְעָה גוּפֵי עֲבֵירוֹת מִקְצָתָן מְעַשְּׂרִין וּמִקְצָתָן אֵינָן מְעַשְּׂרִין רָעָב שֶׁלַּבַּצּוֹרֶת בָּא מִקְצָתָן רְעֵבִים וּמִקְצָתָן שְׂבֵיעִים גָּמְרוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְעַשֵּׂר רָעָב שֶׁלִּמְהוּמָה וְשֶׁלַּבַּצּוֹרֶת בָּא שֶּלֹּא לִיטּוֹל חַלָּה רָעָב שֶׁלְּכַלָּיָה בָא: דֶּבֶר בָּא לָעוֹלָם עַל המִּיתוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁלֹּא נִימְסְרוּ לְבֵית דִּין וְעַל פֵּירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית חֶרֶב בָּאָה לָעוֹלָם עַל עִינּוּי הַדִּין וְעַל עִיוּוּת הַדִּין וְעַל הַמּוֹרִים בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁלֹּא כַהֲלָכָה
sentences.tr: Shiv'a minei pur'aniyot ba'im al shiv'a gufei aveirot. Miktsatan me'asrin u-miktsatan einan me'asrin — ra'av shel batsoret ba: miktsatan re'evim u-miktsatan sve'im. Gamru she-lo le'aser — ra'av shel mehuma ve-shel batsoret ba. She-lo litol ḥala — ra'av shel kelaya ba. Dever ba la-olam al ha-mitot ha-amurot ba-tora she-lo nimseru le-veit din, ve-al peirot shvi'it. Ḥerev ba'a la-olam al inuy ha-din, ve-al ivut ha-din, ve-al ha-morim ba-tora she-lo ka-halakha.
sentences.l: Seven kinds of punishments come for seven bodies of transgressions. Some of them tithe and some of them do not tithe — a famine of drought comes: some of them hungry and some of them sated. They resolved not to tithe — a famine of tumult and of drought comes. (They resolved) not to take ḥalla — a famine of annihilation comes. Pestilence comes to the world for the deaths stated in the Torah that were not handed to a court, and for the fruits of the seventh-year. Sword comes to the world for the affliction of judgment, and for the perversion of judgment, and for those who teach in the Torah not according to the law.
sentences.i: Seven kinds of punishment come for seven main kinds of transgression. When some people tithe and others do not, a famine of drought comes: some go hungry and some are full. When they have resolved not to tithe at all, a famine of turmoil and drought comes. When they resolve not to set aside ḥalla, a famine of annihilation comes. Pestilence comes upon the world for the capital crimes stated in the Torah that were not given over to a court, and for misuse of the produce of the Sabbatical year. The sword comes upon the world for justice delayed, for justice perverted, and for those who teach the Torah contrary to the law.
sentences.n: גּוּפֵי עֲבֵירוֹת, 'bodies of transgressions', means the main categories. Tithes and ḥalla (the portion of dough given to a priest, Numbers 15:20) are owed from food, and withholding them brings famine — punishment to match the crime. A famine 'of tumult' comes with war and disorder. The 'deaths not handed to a court' are crimes the Torah punishes with death that no human court executes: the commentators explain them as left to Heaven. Produce of the seventh year (שְׁבִיעִית, the Sabbatical year) was ownerless and could not be traded. עִינּוּי הַדִּין, 'afflicting justice', is a court that drags out a case. The scribe joins שֶׁל to the following word throughout (שֶׁלַּבַּצּוֹרֶת), and wrote a he at the end of בַּצּוֹרֶת that was corrected to tav. דּבר is unpointed apart from its dagesh: read דֶּבֶר. Kaufmann starts a new section at דֶּבֶר; the printed editions start 5:9 at חַיָּה רָעָה, as here. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: מְעַשְּׂרִין, דֶּבֶר.

sentences.t: חַיָּה רָעָה בָאָה לַעוֹלָם עַל שְׁבוּעַת שָׁוְא וְעַל חִילּוּל הַשֵּׁם גָּלוּת בָּאָה לָעוֹלָם עַל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְעַל גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וְעַל שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים וְעַל הַשְׁמֵט הָאָרֶץ: בְּאַרְבָּעָה פְרָקִים הַדֶּבֶר מְרוּבֶּה בָּרְבִיעִית וּבַשְׁבִיעִית ובְמוֹצָאֵי שְׁבִיעִית וּבְמוֹצָאֵי הֶחָג שֶׁבְּכָל שָׁנָה בָּרְבִיעִית מִפְּנֵי מַעֲשֵׂר עָנִי שֶׁבַּשְּׁלִישִׁית בַּשְּׁבִיעִית מִפְּנֵי מַעֲשֵׂר עָנִי שֶׁבַּשִּׁישִּׁית בְּמוֹצָאֵי שְׁבִיעִית מִפְּנֵי פֵירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית בְמוֹצָאֵי הֶחָג שֶׁבְּכָל שָׁנָה מִפְּנֵי גֶזֶל מַתְּנוֹת עֲנִיִּים:
sentences.tr: Ḥaya ra'a ba'a la-olam al shvu'at shav ve-al ḥilul ha-shem. Galut ba'a la-olam al avoda zara, ve-al gilui arayot, ve-al shfikhut damim, ve-al hashmet ha-arets. Be-arba'a prakim ha-dever merube: ba-revi'it, u-va-shvi'it, u-ve-motsa'ei shvi'it, u-ve-motsa'ei he-ḥag she-be-khol shana. Ba-revi'it — mipnei ma'aser ani she-ba-shlishit; ba-shvi'it — mipnei ma'aser ani she-ba-shishit; be-motsa'ei shvi'it — mipnei peirot shvi'it; be-motsa'ei he-ḥag she-be-khol shana — mipnei gezel matnot aniyim.
sentences.l: A bad beast comes to the world for an oath of vanity and for profanation of the Name. Exile comes to the world for strange worship, and for uncovering of nakedness, and for shedding of blood, and for the release of the land. At four seasons the pestilence is increased: in the fourth, and in the seventh, and at the going-out of the seventh, and at the going-out of the Festival that is in every year. In the fourth — because of the tithe of the poor that is in the third; in the seventh — because of the tithe of the poor that is in the sixth; at the going-out of the seventh — because of the fruits of the seventh; at the going-out of the Festival that is in every year — because of robbery of the gifts of the poor.
sentences.i: Wild beasts come upon the world for false oaths and for profaning the Name. Exile comes upon the world for idolatry, for sexual transgression, for bloodshed, and for working the land in its year of release. At four times pestilence increases: in the fourth year, in the seventh year, at the close of the seventh year, and at the close of the Festival every year. In the fourth year, because of the poor man's tithe of the third; in the seventh, because of the poor man's tithe of the sixth; at the close of the seventh, because of the produce of the Sabbatical year; and at the close of the Festival every year, because the poor were robbed of their gifts.
sentences.n: The four sins that bring exile are idolatry, forbidden sexual unions (גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת, 'uncovering of nakedness', the language of Leviticus 18), bloodshed, and farming the land in the seventh year; Leviticus 26:34–35 says the land will make up its Sabbaths while Israel is in exile. 'The name' (הַשֵּׁם) is God's name. The poor man's tithe fell due in the third and sixth years of the seven-year cycle; pestilence comes the following year if it was withheld. 'The Festival' (הֶחָג) is Sukkot, by which time the gleanings and field-corners owed to the poor have been gathered. Kaufmann reads הַשְׁמֵט הָאָרֶץ, 'the release of the land', where the printed texts have שְׁמִטַּת הָאָרֶץ. In the list of four, the vav of וּבַשְׁבִיעִית is a raised letter and the vav of ובְמוֹצָאֵי was added by a second hand; בַּשְּׁבִיעִית in the second list is written over an erasure. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: וּבְמוֹצָאֵי, מַעֲשֵׂר.

sentences.t: אַרְבַּע מִידּוֹת בָּאָדָם הָאוֹמֵר שֶׁלִּי שֶׁלִּי וְשֶׁלָּךְ שֶׁלָּךְ זוֹ מִידָּה בֵינוֹנִית וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְ׳ זוֹ מִידַּת סְדוֹם שֶׁלִּי שֶׁלָּךְ וְשֶׁלָּךְ שֶׁלִי עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁלִּי שֶׁלָּךְ וְשֶׁלָּךְ שֶׁלָּךְ חָסִיד שֶׁלָּךְ שלי וְשֶׁלִּי שֶׁלִּי רָשָׁע:
sentences.tr: Arba midot ba-adam. Ha-omer: sheli sheli ve-shelakh shelakh — zo mida beinonit; ve-yesh omrim: zo midat Sdom. Sheli shelakh ve-shelakh sheli — am ha-arets. Sheli shelakh ve-shelakh shelakh — ḥasid. Shelakh sheli ve-sheli sheli — rasha.
sentences.l: Four types (are) among people. The one who says: mine (is) mine and yours (is) yours — this is a middling type; and some say: this is the type of Sodom. Mine (is) yours and yours (is) mine — a people-of-the-land. Mine (is) yours and yours (is) yours — a pious-man. Yours (is) mine and mine (is) mine — a wicked-man.
sentences.i: There are four types of people. One who says, 'What is mine is mine and what is yours is yours' — this is the ordinary type; some say it is the way of Sodom. 'What is mine is yours and what is yours is mine' — an ignoramus. 'What is mine is yours and what is yours is yours' — a saint. 'What is yours is mine and what is mine is mine' — a wicked man.
sentences.n: מִידָּה is a measure, and from that a type or trait. In rabbinic tradition Sodom's sin was refusing to share even what cost nothing to give. עַם הָאָרֶץ, literally 'people of the land', is the rabbinic term for an unlearned man; here he is the one who erases the line between mine and yours. Three hands wrote this mishnah in Kaufmann. In the third case the scribe wrote only 'mine is yours'; a second hand rewrote it, and a third made it 'mine is yours and yours is yours'. In the fourth the scribe wrote 'and yours is mine'; the second and third hands produced 'yours is mine and mine is mine'. The text here is the third hand's, which agrees with the printed editions. שלי was left unvocalized, and both זוֹ were added between the lines. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: חָסִיד.
sentences.say: אַרְבַּע מִידּוֹת בָּאָדָם הָאוֹמֵר שֶׁלִּי שֶׁלִּי וְשֶׁלָּךְ שֶׁלָּךְ זוֹ מִידָּה בֵינוֹנִית וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים זוֹ מִידַּת סְדוֹם שֶׁלִּי שֶׁלָּךְ וְשֶׁלָּךְ שֶׁלִי עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁלִּי שֶׁלָּךְ וְשֶׁלָּךְ שֶׁלָּךְ חָסִיד שֶׁלָּךְ שלי וְשֶׁלִּי שֶׁלִּי רָשָׁע:

sentences.t: אַרְבַּע מִידּוֹת בַּדֵּעוֹת נֹוַח לִכְעוֹס וְנֹוַח לִרְצוֹת יָצָא שְׂכָרוֹ בַהֶפְסֵדוֹ קָשֵׁה לִכְעוֹס וְקָשֵׁה לִרְצוֹת יָצָא הֵפְסְדוֹ בִשְׂכָרוֹ קָשֵׁה לִכְעוס וְנֹוַח לִרְצוֹת חָסִיד נֹוַח לִכְעוֹס וְקָשֵׁה לִרְצוֹת רָשָׁע:
sentences.tr: Arba midot ba-de'ot. Noaḥ likh'os ve-noaḥ lirtsot — yatsa skharo ba-hefsedo. Kashe likh'os ve-kashe lirtsot — yatsa hefsedo bi-skharo. Kashe likh'os ve-noaḥ lirtsot — ḥasid. Noaḥ likh'os ve-kashe lirtsot — rasha.
sentences.l: Four types among temperaments. Easy to anger and easy to appease — his gain goes-out in his loss. Hard to anger and hard to appease — his loss goes-out in his gain. Hard to anger and easy to appease — pious. Easy to anger and hard to appease — wicked.
sentences.i: There are four kinds of temperament. Quick to anger and quick to be appeased — his gain is cancelled by his loss. Slow to anger and slow to be appeased — his loss is cancelled by his gain. Slow to anger and quick to be appeased — a saint. Quick to anger and slow to be appeased — a wicked man.
sentences.n: יָצָא שְׂכָרוֹ בְּהֶפְסֵדוֹ, 'his gain goes out in his loss', is a merchant's phrase: the profit goes to cover the loss and he ends level. You will see it again in the next mishnah. דֵּעוֹת here means dispositions. נֹוַח, 'easy', is spelled like Noah's name in 5:2, with a vav after the ḥolam. In Kaufmann מִידּוֹת was added in the margin, and the scribe's false start בדיעת was erased.

sentences.t: אַרְבַּע מִידּוֹת בַּלְּמֵידִים מְמַהֵר לִשְׁמֹוַע וּמְמַהֵר לְאַבֵּד יָצָא שְׂכָרוֹ בַהֵפְסֵדֹו קָשֶׁה לִשְׁמוֹע וְקָשֶׁה לְאָבֵּד יָצָא הֵפְסֵדוֹ בִשְׂכָרוֹ מְמַהֵר לִשְׁמֹוַע וְקָשֶׁה לְאַבֵּד חָכָם קָשֶׁה לִשְׁמֹוַע וּמְמַהֵר לְאַבֵּד זֶה חֵלֶק רַע:
sentences.tr: Arba midot ba-lmeidim. Memaher lishmoa u-memaher le'abed — yatsa skharo ba-hefsedo. Kashe lishmoa ve-kashe le'abed — yatsa hefsedo bi-skharo. Memaher lishmoa ve-kashe le'abed — ḥakham. Kashe lishmoa u-memaher le'abed — ze ḥelek ra.
sentences.l: Four types among learners. Quick to hear and quick to lose — his gain goes-out in his loss. Hard to hear and hard to lose — his loss goes-out in his gain. Quick to hear and hard to lose — wise. Hard to hear and quick to lose — this is a bad portion.
sentences.i: There are four kinds of students. Quick to grasp and quick to forget — his gain is cancelled by his loss. Slow to grasp and slow to forget — his loss is cancelled by his gain. Quick to grasp and slow to forget — a wise man. Slow to grasp and quick to forget — that is a bad lot.
sentences.n: לִשְׁמוֹעַ, 'to hear', is to take in a teaching; לְאַבֵּד, 'to lose', is to forget it. Teaching was oral: a student heard a lesson and kept it in his memory. Kaufmann has לְמֵידִים, 'learners', a form from the root of לָמַד, where the printed editions have תַּלְמִידִים. It writes לִשְׁמֹוַע with a vav after the ḥolam, as in נֹוַח.

sentences.t: אַרְבַּע מִידּוֹת בְּנוֹתְנֵי צְדָקָה רוֹצֶה שֶׁיִּתֵּן וְאַל יִתְּנוּ אֲחֵרִים עֵינוֹ רָעָה בְּשֶׁלַּאֲחֵרִים שֶׁיִּתְּנוּ אֲחֵרִים וְהוּא לֹא יִתֵּן עֵינוֹ רָעָה בְשֶׁלּוֹ שֶׁיִּתֵּן וְיִתְּנוּ אֲחֵרִים חָסִיד אַל יִתַּן וְאַל יִתְּנוּ אֲחֵרִים רָשָׁע:
sentences.tr: Arba midot be-notnei tsdaka. Rotse she-yiten ve-al yitnu aḥerim — eino ra'a be-shel aḥerim. She-yitnu aḥerim ve-hu lo yiten — eino ra'a be-shelo. She-yiten ve-yitnu aḥerim — ḥasid. Al yitan ve-al yitnu aḥerim — rasha.
sentences.l: Four types among givers of charity. (One who) wants that he give and that others not give — his eye is bad toward what-is-of others. That others give and he not give — his eye is bad toward what-is-his. That he give and others give — pious. (That) he not give and others not give — wicked.
sentences.i: There are four kinds of givers of charity. One who wants to give but wants others not to give begrudges others what is theirs. One who wants others to give but will not give himself begrudges what is his own. One who gives and wants others to give is a saint. One who will not give and wants others not to give is a wicked man.
sentences.n: עַיִן רָעָה, 'a bad eye', is stinginess, the grudging look at what someone has. The first giver grudges others the merit and credit their giving would earn them; the second grudges his own money. In Kaufmann the shin of שיִּתְּנוּ was added above the line, unvocalized, and the שֶׁ of the next שֶׁיִּתֵּן was added in the margin by a second hand. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: שֶׁיִּתְּנוּ.

sentences.t: אַרְבַּע מִידּוֹת בְּהוֹלְכֵי לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ הוֹלֵךְ וְאֵינוּ עוֹשֶׂה שְׂכַר הֲלִיכָה בְיָדוֹ עוֹשֶׂה וְאֵינוּ הוֹלֵךְ שְׂכַר מַעֲשֶׂה בְיָדוֹ הוֹלֵךְ וְעוֹשֶׂה חָסִיד לֹא הוֹלֵךְ וְלֹא עוֹשֶׂה רָשָׁע:
sentences.tr: Arba midot be-holkhei le-veit ha-midrash. Holekh ve-einu ose — skhar halikha be-yado. Ose ve-einu holekh — skhar ma'ase be-yado. Holekh ve-ose — ḥasid. Lo holekh ve-lo ose — rasha.
sentences.l: Four types among goers to the house of study. Goes and does not do — the reward of going (is) in his hand. Does and does not go — the reward of doing (is) in his hand. Goes and does — pious. Does not go and does not do — wicked.
sentences.i: There are four kinds among those who go to the house of study. One who goes but does not practise has the reward for going. One who practises but does not go has the reward for practising. One who goes and practises is a saint. One who neither goes nor practises is a wicked man.
sentences.n: בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ is the study house where the sages taught. 'Doing' may mean studying once he gets there, or putting what he hears into practice; commentators read it both ways. 'In his hand' means he holds it: the reward is his.

sentences.t: אַרְבַּע מִידּוֹת בְּיוֹשְׁבֵי לִפְנֵי חֲכָמִ׳ סְפוֹג מַשְׁפֵּךְ וּמְשַׁמֶּרֶת וְנָפָה סְפוֹג שֶׁהוּא סוֹפֵג אֶת הַכֹּל מַשְׁפֵּךְ שֶׁהוּא מַכְנִיס בָּזוֹ וּמוֹצִיא בָזוֹ מְשַׁמֶּרֶת שֶׁהִיא מוֹצִיאָה אֶת הַיַּיִן וְקוֹלֶטֶת אֶת הַשְּׁמָרִים נָפָה שֶׂהִיא מוֹצִיאָה אֶת הַקֶּמַח וְקוֹלֶטֶת אֶת הַסֹּלֶת:
sentences.tr: Arba midot be-yoshvei lifnei ḥakhamim: sfog, mashpekh, u-mshameret, ve-nafa. Sfog — she-hu sofeg et ha-kol. Mashpekh — she-hu makhnis ba-zo u-motsi va-zo. Meshameret — she-hi motsi'a et ha-yayin ve-kolet et ha-shmarim. Nafa — she-hi motsi'a et ha-kemaḥ ve-kolet et ha-solet.
sentences.l: Four types among sitters before sages: sponge, funnel, and strainer, and sieve. Sponge — that it soaks-up everything. Funnel — that it brings-in at this and lets-out at this. Strainer — that it lets-out the wine and catches the lees. Sieve — that it lets-out the flour and catches the fine-flour.
sentences.i: There are four kinds among those who sit before the sages: the sponge, the funnel, the strainer, and the sieve. The sponge soaks up everything. The funnel takes in at one end and lets out at the other. The strainer lets the wine through and keeps back the dregs. The sieve lets the flour-dust through and keeps back the fine flour.
sentences.n: Each image describes what a student keeps. The sponge keeps everything, good and bad alike; the funnel keeps nothing; the strainer keeps the dregs and lets the wine go; the sieve keeps the best. קֶמַח here is the powdery meal that falls through the sieve, סֹלֶת the choice flour it holds back. בָּזוֹ … בָזוֹ, 'at this … at this', means 'at one end … at the other'. חֲכָמִ׳ is abbreviated. In Kaufmann a final mem after בְּיוֹשְׁבֵי was erased, and שֶׂהִיא carries a sin dot, a slip for שֶׁהִיא.
sentences.say: אַרְבַּע מִידּוֹת בְּיוֹשְׁבֵי לִפְנֵי חֲכָמִים סְפוֹג מַשְׁפֵּךְ וּמְשַׁמֶּרֶת וְנָפָה סְפוֹג שֶׁהוּא סוֹפֵג אֶת הַכֹּל מַשְׁפֵּךְ שֶׁהוּא מַכְנִיס בָּזוֹ וּמוֹצִיא בָזוֹ מְשַׁמֶּרֶת שֶׁהִיא מוֹצִיאָה אֶת הַיַּיִן וְקוֹלֶטֶת אֶת הַשְּׁמָרִים נָפָה שֶׂהִיא מוֹצִיאָה אֶת הַקֶּמַח וְקוֹלֶטֶת אֶת הַסֹּלֶת:

sentences.t: כָּל אַהֲבָה שֶׁהִיא תְלוּיָיה בְדָבָר בָּטֵל דָּבָר וּבָטֵילָה אַהֲבָה וְשֶׁאֵינָה תְלוּיָה בְדָבָר אֵינָה בְטֵילָה לְעוֹלָם: אֵי זה הִיא אַהֲבָה שֶׁהִיא תְלוּיָיה בְדָבָר זו אַהֲבַת אַמְנוֹן וְתָמָר וְשֶׁאֵינָה תְלוּיָה בְדָבָר זוֹ אַהֲבַת דָּוִד וִיהוֹנָתָן:
sentences.tr: Kol ahava she-hi tluya be-davar — batel davar u-vateila ahava. Ve-she-eina tluya be-davar — eina vteila le-olam. Ei ze hi ahava she-hi tluya be-davar? Zo ahavat Amnon ve-Tamar. Ve-she-eina tluya be-davar? Zo ahavat David vi-Yhonatan.
sentences.l: Every love that is dependent on a thing — (when) the thing ceases, the love ceases. And (love) that is not dependent on a thing does not cease, ever. Which is love that is dependent on a thing? This is the love of Amnon and Tamar. And that is not dependent on a thing? This is the love of David and Jonathan.
sentences.i: Any love that depends on something passes when that thing passes; love that depends on nothing never passes. What is love that depends on something? The love of Amnon for Tamar. And love that depends on nothing? The love of David and Jonathan.
sentences.n: Amnon desired his half-sister Tamar, raped her, and then hated her more than he had loved her (2 Samuel 13:15). Jonathan loved David 'as his own soul' (1 Samuel 18:1), though David stood to take the throne Jonathan would have inherited. בָּטֵל, 'is void, ceases', is a legal word. תְלוּיָיה shows the manuscript's doubled yod. Kaufmann begins a new section at אֵי זֶה הִיא; the printed editions keep it all as one mishnah. Both זוֹ were added in the margin by a second hand.

sentences.t: כַּל מַחֲלוֹקֶת שֶׁהִיא לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם סוֹפָה לְהִתְקַיֵּים וְשֶׁאֵינָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם אֵין סוֹפָהּ לְהִתְקַיֵּים: אֵי זוֹ הִיא מַחֲלוֹקֶת שֶׁהִיא לְשֵם שָׁמַיִם מַחֲלוֹקֶת שַמַּי וְהֶלֵּל וְשֶׁאֵינָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם זוֹ מַחֲלוֹקְתּוֹ שֶׁלְּקֹרַח:
sentences.tr: Kol maḥloket she-hi le-shem shamayim sofa lehitkayem, ve-she-eina le-shem shamayim ein sofa lehitkayem. Ei zo hi maḥloket she-hi le-shem shamayim? Maḥloket Shamay ve-Helel. Ve-she-eina le-shem shamayim? Zo maḥalokto shel Koraḥ.
sentences.l: Every dispute that is for the name of Heaven — its end (is) to endure; and that is not for the name of Heaven — its end (is) not to endure. Which is a dispute that is for the name of Heaven? The dispute of Shammai and Hillel. And that is not for the name of Heaven? This is the dispute of Korah.
sentences.i: Every dispute for the sake of Heaven will endure in the end, and one not for the sake of Heaven will not endure in the end. What is a dispute for the sake of Heaven? The dispute of Shammai and Hillel. And one not for the sake of Heaven? The dispute of Korah.
sentences.n: The disputes of the houses of Shammai and Hillel run through the whole Mishnah, and both sides' views are recorded and studied to this day: that is how they endure. Korah led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron that ended with the earth swallowing him (Numbers 16). Kaufmann names Shammai before Hillel, where the printed editions put Hillel first, and has 'the dispute of Korah' where the printed text adds 'and all his congregation'. Kaufmann begins a new section at אֵי זוֹ הִיא. לְשֵׁם in the second half was added in the margin, and the vav of מַחֲלוֹקְתּוֹ by a second hand.

sentences.t: כָּל הַמְזַכֶּה אֶת הָרַבִּים אֵין חֵט בָּאָה עַל יָדוֹ וְכָל הַמַּחֲטִיא אֶת הָרַבִּים אֵין מַסְפִּיקִין בְּיָדוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה: מֹשֶׁה זָכָה וְזִיכָּה אֶת הָרַבִּים וּזְכוּת הָרַבִּים תְּלוּיָה בוֹ שנ׳ צִדְקַת יָ׳י עָשָׂה וּמִשְׁפָּטָיו עִם יש׳ יָרָבְעָם חָטָא וְהֶחֱטִיא אֶת הָרַבִּים וְחֵטְא הָרַבִּים תְּלוּיָה בוֹ שנ׳ עַל חַטֹּאת יָרָבְעָם אֲשֶׁר חָטָא וַאֲשֶׁר הֶחֱטִיא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ׳
sentences.tr: Kol ha-mezake et ha-rabim ein ḥet ba'a al yado, ve-khol ha-maḥati et ha-rabim ein maspikin be-yado la'asot tshuva. Moshe zakha ve-zika et ha-rabim — u-zkhut ha-rabim tluya vo, she-ne'emar: tsidkat Adonay asa u-mishpatav im Yisra'el. Yarov'am ḥata ve-heḥeti et ha-rabim — ve-ḥet ha-rabim tluya vo, she-ne'emar: al ḥatot Yarov'am asher ḥata va-asher heḥeti et Yisra'el.
sentences.l: Whoever brings-merit to the many — sin does not come by his hand; and whoever causes-to-sin the many — they do not supply into his hand to do repentance. Moses gained-merit and brought-merit to the many; the merit of the many hangs on him, as it is said: the righteousness of the LORD he did, and His judgments with Israel. Jeroboam sinned and caused-to-sin the many; the sin of the many hangs on him, as it is said: for the sins of Jeroboam which he sinned and which he caused Israel to sin.
sentences.i: Whoever leads the many to merit will not be the cause of sin; whoever leads the many into sin is given no chance to repent. Moses gained merit and led the many to merit, so the merit of the many is credited to him, as it is said: 'He carried out the LORD's righteousness and His judgments with Israel' (Deuteronomy 33:21). Jeroboam sinned and led the many into sin, so the sin of the many is charged to him, as it is said: 'For the sins of Jeroboam, which he sinned and which he caused Israel to sin' (1 Kings 15:30).
sentences.n: זִיכָּה אֶת הָרַבִּים, 'brought merit to the many', means leading the public to do right. אֵין מַסְפִּיקִין בְּיָדוֹ: Heaven does not give him the means to repent. The commentators explain why: he should not end in paradise while the people he misled end in Gehenna. Jeroboam set up the golden calves at Bethel and Dan (1 Kings 12:28–30). Kaufmann writes חֵט without alef in the first line and treats it, and חֵטְא later, as feminine (בָּאָה, תְּלוּיָה). יָ׳י is the scribe's sign for the divine name; יש׳ abbreviates יִשְׂרָאֵל. A second hand added the yod of הַמַּחֲטִיא. Kaufmann begins a new section at מֹשֶׁה.
sentences.say: כָּל הַמְזַכֶּה אֶת הָרַבִּים אֵין חֵט בָּאָה עַל יָדוֹ וְכָל הַמַּחֲטִיא אֶת הָרַבִּים אֵין מַסְפִּיקִין בְּיָדוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה: מֹשֶׁה זָכָה וְזִיכָּה אֶת הָרַבִּים וּזְכוּת הָרַבִּים תְּלוּיָה בוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר צִדְקַת אֲדֹנָי עָשָׂה וּמִשְׁפָּטָיו עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל יָרָבְעָם חָטָא וְהֶחֱטִיא אֶת הָרַבִּים וְחֵטְא הָרַבִּים תְּלוּיָה בוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר עַל חַטֹּאת יָרָבְעָם אֲשֶׁר חָטָא וַאֲשֶׁר הֶחֱטִיא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל

sentences.t: כָּל שֶׁיֶּש בּוֹ שְׁלוֹשָה דְבָרִים תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁלְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁלְּבִלְעָם עַיִן טוֹבָה וְנֶפֶשׁ שְׁפָלָה וְרוּחַ נְמוּכָה תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁלְּאַבְרָהָם עַיִן רָעָה וְנֶפֶשׁ רְחָבָה וְרוּחַ גְּבוֹהָה תַלְמִידוֹ שלבלעם מה בין תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁלְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ לְתַלְמִידָיו שֶׁלְּבִלְעָם תַּלְמִידָיו שֶׁלְּבִלְעָם יוֹרְדִים לְגֵיהִינָּם שנ׳ וְאַתָּה אֱלֹהִים תּוֹרִידֵם לִבְאֵר שַׁחַת אַנְשֵׁי רָמִים וּמִרְמָה לֹא יֶחֱצוּ יְמֵיהֶם וַאֲנִי אֶבְטַח בָּךְ אֲבַל תַּלְמִידָיו שֶׁלְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ יוֹרְשִׁים לְגַן עֵדֶן שנ׳ לְהַנְחִיל אֹהֲבַי יֵשׁ וְאוֹצְרוֹתֵיהֶם אֲמַלֵּא
sentences.tr: Kol she-yesh bo shlosha dvarim — talmido shel Avraham avinu; u-shlosha dvarim — talmido shel Bil'am. Ayin tova, ve-nefesh shfela, ve-ruaḥ nemukha — talmido shel Avraham. Ayin ra'a, ve-nefesh reḥava, ve-ruaḥ gvoha — talmido shel Bil'am. Ma bein talmido shel Avraham avinu le-talmidav shel Bil'am? Talmidav shel Bil'am yordim le-Geihinam, she-ne'emar: ve-ata Elohim toridem li-v'er shaḥat, anshei ramim u-mirma lo yeḥetsu yemeihem, va-ani evtaḥ bakh. Aval talmidav shel Avraham avinu yorshim le-Gan Eden, she-ne'emar: lehanḥil ohavai yesh, ve-otsroteihem amale.
sentences.l: Anyone who has in him three things — (he is) a disciple of Abraham our father; and three things — a disciple of Balaam. A good eye, and a low soul, and a humble spirit — a disciple of Abraham. A bad eye, and a wide soul, and a high spirit — a disciple of Balaam. What (is) between a disciple of Abraham our father and the disciples of Balaam? The disciples of Balaam go-down to Gehenna, as it is said: and You, God, will bring-them-down to the well of the pit; men of haughtiness and deceit shall not halve their days; and I will trust in You. But the disciples of Abraham our father inherit the Garden of Eden, as it is said: to make those who love Me inherit substance, and their treasuries I will fill.
sentences.i: Whoever has these three qualities is a disciple of Abraham our father; whoever has three others is a disciple of Balaam. A generous eye, a modest appetite, and a humble spirit — a disciple of Abraham. A grudging eye, a greedy appetite, and a proud spirit — a disciple of Balaam. What is the difference between the disciples of Abraham our father and the disciples of Balaam? The disciples of Balaam go down to Gehenna, as it is said: 'And You, O God, will bring them down to the pit of destruction; the haughty and deceitful shall not live out half their days; but I will trust in You' (Psalms 55:24). The disciples of Abraham our father inherit the Garden of Eden, as it is said: 'To endow those who love Me with substance, and I will fill their treasuries' (Proverbs 8:21).
sentences.n: Balaam, the seer hired to curse Israel (Numbers 22–24), is the rabbinic type of a gifted man spoiled by greed and pride, and Abraham is his opposite. A 'good eye' is generosity; נֶפֶשׁ here is appetite, 'low' when modest and 'wide' when greedy. In the Proverbs verse יֵשׁ, 'there is', is read as a noun: 'substance, something real'. Gehenna is the place of punishment after death. Kaufmann reads רָמִים, 'haughty', in the psalm, where the biblical text has דָמִים, 'blood' — dalet and resh look alike, and 'haughty' suits Balaam's high spirit. The printed editions differ in several ways: they have 'of the disciples of' (plural), call him 'Balaam the wicked', put Abraham's disciples first, and add that they 'eat (the fruits) in this world'. אֹהֲבַי was added in the margin; שלבלעם is unvocalized.
sentences.say: כָּל שֶׁיֶּש בּוֹ שְׁלוֹשָה דְבָרִים תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁלְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁלְּבִלְעָם עַיִן טוֹבָה וְנֶפֶשׁ שְׁפָלָה וְרוּחַ נְמוּכָה תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁלְּאַבְרָהָם עַיִן רָעָה וְנֶפֶשׁ רְחָבָה וְרוּחַ גְּבוֹהָה תַלְמִידוֹ שלבלעם מה בין תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁלְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ לְתַלְמִידָיו שֶׁלְּבִלְעָם תַּלְמִידָיו שֶׁלְּבִלְעָם יוֹרְדִים לְגֵיהִינָּם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְאַתָּה אֱלֹהִים תּוֹרִידֵם לִבְאֵר שַׁחַת אַנְשֵׁי רָמִים וּמִרְמָה לֹא יֶחֱצוּ יְמֵיהֶם וַאֲנִי אֶבְטַח בָּךְ אֲבַל תַּלְמִידָיו שֶׁלְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ יוֹרְשִׁים לְגַן עֵדֶן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לְהַנְחִיל אֹהֲבַי יֵשׁ וְאוֹצְרוֹתֵיהֶם אֲמַלֵּא

sentences.t: יְהוּדָה בֶן תֵימָה אוֹמֵ׳ הֱוֵוי עָז כַּנָּמֵר וְקַל כַּנֶּשֶׁר וְרָץ כַּצְּבִי וְגִיבּוֹר כַּאֲרִי לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן אָבִיךָ שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵ׳ עַז פָּנִים לְגֵיהִינָּם וּבוֹשׁ פָּנִים לְגַן עֵדֶן יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ יָ׳י אֱ׳הֵינוּ וא׳הֵי אֲבוֹתֵי׳ שֶׁתִּבְנֶה עִירָךְ בְּיָמֵינוּ וְתִתֵּן חֶלְקֵינוּ בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ:
sentences.tr: Yehuda ben Teima omer: hevei az ka-namer, ve-kal ka-nesher, ve-rats ka-tsvi, ve-gibor ka-ari, la'asot retson avikha she-ba-shamayim. Hu haya omer: az panim le-Geihinam, u-vosh panim le-Gan Eden. Yehi ratson milfanekha, Adonay Eloheinu ve-Elohei avoteinu, she-tivne irakh be-yameinu, ve-titen ḥelkeinu be-toratekha.
sentences.l: Judah son of Tema says: be bold as the leopard, and light as the eagle, and running as the gazelle, and mighty as the lion, to do the will of your Father who is in heaven. He was saying: the bold of face — to Gehenna; and the shamed of face — to the Garden of Eden. May it be the will before You, LORD our God and God of our fathers, that You build Your city in our days, and give our portion in Your Torah.
sentences.i: Judah ben Tema says: Be bold as a leopard, light as an eagle, swift as a gazelle, and strong as a lion, to do the will of your Father in heaven. He used to say: The brazen are bound for Gehenna, and the shamefaced for the Garden of Eden. May it be Your will, LORD our God and God of our fathers, that You rebuild Your city in our days, and grant us our portion in Your Torah.
sentences.n: עַז פָּנִים, 'strong of face', is brazenness; בּוֹשׁ פָּנִים, 'shamefaced', is the modesty that holds a person back from sin. The closing prayer asks for Jerusalem to be rebuilt. The printed prayer has בִּמְהֵרָה, 'speedily', before 'in our days'. The divine names are abbreviated: יָ׳י, אֱ׳הֵינוּ and א׳הֵי, and אֲבוֹתֵי׳ for אֲבוֹתֵינוּ. A tav was erased at the end of וּבוֹשׁ (the printed text has בֹּשֶׁת פָּנִים). Kaufmann begins a new section at הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ.
sentences.say: יְהוּדָה בֶן תֵימָה אוֹמֵר הֱוֵוי עָז כַּנָּמֵר וְקַל כַּנֶּשֶׁר וְרָץ כַּצְּבִי וְגִיבּוֹר כַּאֲרִי לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן אָבִיךָ שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר עַז פָּנִים לְגֵיהִינָּם וּבוֹשׁ פָּנִים לְגַן עֵדֶן יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ אֲדֹנָי אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁתִּבְנֶה עִירָךְ בְּיָמֵינוּ וְתִתֵּן חֶלְקֵינוּ בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ:

sentences.t: בֶּן בַּגְבַּג אוֹמֵ׳ הֲפֹך בָּהּ וְהַפֵּךְ בָּהּ דְכוֹלָהּ בָךְ וְכוֹלָּךְ בָּהּ וּבַה תְּיהוֵי וּמֶנָּה לָא תֵזוּעַ שֶׁאֵין לָךְ מִידָּה טוֹבָה מִמֶּנָּה
sentences.tr: Ben Bagbag omer: hafokh bah ve-hapekh bah, de-khulah vakh ve-khulakh bah; u-vah tehevei, u-menah la tezua, she-ein lakh mida tova mimena.
sentences.l: Ben Bagbag says: turn it and turn it, for all-of-it (is) in you and all-of-you (is) in it; and in it be, and from it do not move, for you have no measure better than it.
sentences.i: Ben Bagbag says: Turn it over and turn it over again, for all of it is in you and all of you is in it. Stay with it, and do not stray from it, for you have no better portion than this.
sentences.n: 'It' is the Torah. The saying is in Aramaic until its last clause: דְּ 'for', כּוֹלָהּ 'all of it', תְּהֵוֵי 'be', מִנַּהּ 'from it', לָא 'not', תְּזוּעַ 'move'. Kaufmann has no 5:21: the printed saying on the stages of life ('At five years old, to Scripture…') is absent from the manuscript, so the numbering here passes from 5:20 to 5:22. Kaufmann's wording also differs from the printed one, which reads דְּכֹלָּא בַהּ, 'for everything is in it', and adds 'and in it look, and grow old and worn in it'. In the manuscript, 'all of it is in you and all of you is in it' is written over an erasure, so the scribe's own words are lost, and 'and in it be' was added in the margin by a second hand.
sentences.say: בֶּן בַּגְבַּג אוֹמֵר הֲפֹך בָּהּ וְהַפֵּךְ בָּהּ דְכוֹלָהּ בָךְ וְכוֹלָּךְ בָּהּ וּבַה תְּיהוֵי וּמֶנָּה לָא תֵזוּעַ שֶׁאֵין לָךְ מִידָּה טוֹבָה מִמֶּנָּה

sentences.t: בֶּן הֵהֵא אוֹמֵ׳ לְפֻס צַעְרָה אַגְרָה:
sentences.tr: Ben Hehe omer: lefus tsa'ra agra.
sentences.l: Ben Hehe says: according-to the pain, the wage.
sentences.i: Ben Hehe says: The reward matches the effort.
sentences.n: Aramaic: לְפוּם 'according to', צַעֲרָא 'pain, toil', אַגְרָא 'wage'. Kaufmann writes לְפֻס with a final samekh where final mem is expected — the two letters look alike — and the transcriber marks it 'thus!'. The manuscript spells the Aramaic -a ending with he (צַעְרָה, אַגְרָה) where the printed texts have alef, and names the sage Hehe (printed: He He). The tractate ends here: the manuscript closes with חסל אבות, 'Avot is finished'. The sixth chapter of prayer-book editions is a later addition.
sentences.say: בֶּן הֵהֵא אוֹמֵר לְפֻס צַעְרָה אַגְרָה:
